submission.text: r subsequent award should first submit their concern directly to the Contracting Officer, providing sufficient detail to allow the Contracting Officer to understand and assess the issue. Process: The Contracting Officer will review the concern, seek clarification as needed, and engage with the interested party to attempt prompt resolution. Review Timeline: The Contracting Officer will make every effort to provide a response or resolution within 10 business days of receiving the concern. Effect on Award or Performance: Tier 1 engagement is not considered an official notification of filing an agency protest and does not pause solicitation deadlines, delay award decisions, or suspend contract performance. Next Steps: If the matter cannot be resolved at Tier 1, the interested party may file a written agency protest under Tier 2. USDA encourages all parties to seek resolution with the Contracting Officer before filing an agency protest. Tier 2: Agency Protest If concerns cannot be resolved at Tier 1, an interested party may file a written agency protest with either the Contracting Officer or the USDA Independent Review Authority. The decision by the USDA Independent Review Authority is an alternative to a decision by the Contracting Officer. The USDA Independent Review Authority

submission.text: will have one RD wide BAA to monitor on SAM.gov instead of multiple BAAs across the Directorate • Why do we need another contracting tool separate from DETER? • Selecting the right contracting tool for the job leads to the best outcomes. TACTICAL BAA fills a gap for pursuing FAR-based awards for 6.1-6.4 efforts that was not available previously at the directorate level. TACTICAL will complement other tools such as the DETER ARA, SBIR/STTRs, and grants & cooperative agreements under the upcoming RAD Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA). • What if a technically qualified offeror wants to join a Topic Area Group, but missed the normal deadline? • The offeror can either wait and submit during the next annual period (every January) or AFRL can choose to release an interim request for additional executive summaries. • Will these slides be available online or via email? •The slide will be emailed to all registered participants, along with the Q&A, and will also be posted to the sam.gov DETER Virtual Industry Day announcement. • When will the next closed call be released? •Please keep monitoring the TACTICAL SAM.gov posting and sign up for notification of changes. This will notify you when there are changes or a Call announcement is made under TACTICAL. AFRL-2023-4752 Approved

DCC’s Code of Business Conduct covers such issues as values and ethics, standards of conduct and conflict of interest. 5. egotiation or obtaining of the contract if the payment of the fee would require the individual to file a return under section 5 of the Lobbying Act; 5.3.2 corruption, collusion, bid-rigging or any other anti-competitive activity under the Competition Act in the bidding process, real property transactions, the performance of work, the supply of goods or the rendering of services; 5.3.3 any activity that has resulted or could result in being convicted of an offence under any of the provisions listed in the Ineligibility and Suspension Policy. 5.4 S uppliers shall comply with applicable Government of Canada security and confidentiality requirements. 5.5 To help ensure that the entire procurement process conforms to the highest standards of ethical conduct, suppliers are required to avoid any action that would jeopardize the ability of DCC’s employees to respect their obligations under DCC’s Code of Business Conduct . Background: The Hatchery Building was originally constructed in 1962 and consists of unreinforced concrete blocks on concrete stem walls and slab on grade. The roof system consists of open web joists bearing on either masonry walls or wider flanged beams with 5/8” plywood deck and a flat roof. In 1969, an addition was added for lab space on the eastern side of the building. Walls were constructed of 8” block along with open web joists for the roof framing. Repair or replacement of failed or deteriorated equipment outside those tasks is corrective work and requires an itemized quote and prior written authorization from the Contracting Officer under the applicable NTE CLIN or contract modification. For classification only, a minor repair is limited work that does not require major disassembly or replacement of a major component. A major repair involves substantial disassembly, specialized labor or equipment, opening a refrigerant circuit, structural work, or repair or replacement of a major component. sla_onsite.text: Printing's (BEP) Facility located in Washington, DC contains an Industrial Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (WWPP). BEP's objective is to procure contractor services to manage, operate, maintain supplies and perform maintenance and provide technical support for the Wastewater and Storm Water Programs. The WWPP requires services to support the BEP on a 24/7 basis. The WWPP currently consists of four (4) systems: (1) Wiping Solution Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (WSWPP), (2) Plating Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (PWPP), (3) Grease Trap Wastewater Pretreatment Plant (GTWPP), and (4) Wiping Solution Recycling Plant (WSRP). The WWPP includes an on-site lab and a materials storage area. Refer to Attachments 2, 3, 4, and 5 for descriptions of the four (4) systems as well as Attachment 9 and 10 for listings of the equipment that are part of the WSWPP and PWPP, respectively. The GTWPP may be removed during the course of this contract. In addition to these systems, additional systems are currently being researched that will be included in the scope of this requirement.
